title: Resolve bottleneck tasks before picking up new work
directive: Before starting a new task, check whether any open task blocks ≥2 others. If so, prioritise that blocking task.
rationale: Bottleneck tasks multiply their delay across every dependent task.
evidence: Bottleneck tasks (each blocks ≥2 others): TASK-002, TASK-004, TASK-001.

title: Ensure all agent roles have active work
directive: Roles currently without completed tasks (Architect, DevOps Engineer, Core Logic Engineer, Privacy/Networking Engineer, iOS/xrOS Engineer, Android/AR Engineer, Web/WebXR Engineer, Documentation Writer) should be assigned at least one open task. The Task Manager must review TASKS.md weekly and ensure no role is idle for more than 7 days.
rationale: Idle roles indicate imbalanced workload or blocked agents.
evidence: Roles with no completed tasks: Architect, DevOps Engineer, Core Logic Engineer, Privacy/Networking Engineer, iOS/xrOS Engineer, Android/AR Engineer, Web/WebXR Engineer, Documentation Writer.

title: Critical tasks take priority over high/medium tasks
directive: No agent may begin a high or medium priority task if a critical task is available and unblocked. Critical tasks must be fully complete (PR merged) before new high-priority work begins.
rationale: Critical tasks are foundational; delaying them blocks everything else.

title: Every source file must have a corresponding test file
directive: When creating any source file in core/ or services/, immediately create test_<filename> in the same directory. A PR adding source without tests must not be merged.
rationale: Untested code leads to silent regressions, especially in shared core logic.
evidence: 7 source file(s) have no corresponding test file.

title: Every module directory must contain a README.md
directive: When scaffolding any new directory in core/, services/, or platform/, add a README.md explaining the module's purpose, its public API, and how to run its tests.
rationale: Undocumented modules prevent new agents from understanding the codebase.

title: Source files must stay under 500 lines
directive: If a source file exceeds 500 lines, split it into focused sub-modules. Use one file per class / concern. Prefer composition over monoliths.
rationale: Large files are harder to understand, review, and test.
evidence: 4 file(s) exceed 500 lines and may need splitting.

title: Scaffold required directories before implementing features
directive: The first PR for any platform or module must create the directory with a README.md. Never add feature code to a directory that hasn't been formally scaffolded.
rationale: Premature feature code without structure leads to tangled modules.
evidence: 5 required directories do not exist yet.
